title: Persistence is actually useful
scientific_question: Does persistent acquired competence improve future performance beyond giving an agent the same information as history/context?
claim_under_test: An executable, retrievable skill library produces cumulative capability that equal-information context memory does not.
why_prometheus: Engine Five's whole premise. If false, the Voyager mechanism is a context-management trick and needs no engine.
source_mechanism: Voyager SkillManager (name + NL description + executable payload + embedding key; retrieval_top_k=5); Techne source autopsy 2026-09-21
minimum_viable_world: A tiny gridworld/toolchain world with recurring structural regularities (shared sub-procedures) but no repeated task instances; deterministic, seedable, no LLM required for the base controller.
primary_endpoint: tasks solved per unit compute on held-out tasks after a context reset
secondary_endpoints: count of previously unreachable states reached
anticheat: held-out tasks never appear in any prompt or library entry
library contents hashed and diffed against task specs
detect verbatim answer storage (skill payload that encodes the solution rather than a procedure)
falsifier: With information and compute matched, D/E show no advantage over B/C on held-out post-reset competence.
causal_test: late-run library swap: empty / shuffled / equal-size irrelevant / foreign-lineage library; measure competence collapse
telemetry: library adds/updates with parent skill ids
expected_failure_modes: library becomes a lookup table of answers
world regularities too shallow for reuse
assumption_cost: Skill libraries privilege discrete, nameable, reusable procedures; continuous or diffuse competence cannot enter the library and will look like 'no benefit'. Counter-arm: a non-discrete memory (parameter delta) treatment.
prerequisites: a controller that can call stored procedures
donor_code: MineDojo/Voyager MIT, pinned + fossilized (techne/fossils/specimens/voyager-minedojo-2023); SOURCE_ONLY (needs Minecraft client + paid API, not exercised)
implementation_gap: Voyager's payload is JS-in-Minecraft; needs the schema re-hosted on a Prometheus substrate with our own executor. Techne organ 1 (SkillManager schema + versioning + vector retrieval, ~130 lines) is the extraction target.
information_gain: HIGH -- a negative result kills the fifth engine cheaply and redirects the Voyager machinery to a memory feature inside an existing engine.
promotion_gate: D or E beats B/C on the primary endpoint at matched information and compute, in >= 2 world families, with the swap test showing collapse.
stopping_rule: Stop at the preregistered episode budget or when the information-matching control fails audit.

title: Skill composition opens new reachable space
scientific_question: Can independently acquired skills compose into competence that was never directly trained?
claim_under_test: Composition of stored skills reaches goals that neither skill nor the base controller reaches alone.
why_prometheus: Composition, not storage, is what would make a library a substrate for further search (see EV-10).
source_mechanism: Voyager .programs concatenation (stored skills + fixed primitives form the callable language)
minimum_viable_world: Tasks requiring A+B where training exposes A and B separately and the composite never appears.
controls: hand-authored macro as the performance ceiling
composite task withheld from every prompt, library and curriculum
primary_endpoint: zero-shot success on withheld composite tasks
anticheat: composite tasks generated after training and hashed
check retrieval logs for composite leakage
reject runs where a skill's description names the composite
falsifier: Composable and non-composable libraries perform identically on withheld composites.
causal_test: ablate one constituent skill and confirm the composite fails; restore and confirm recovery
expected_failure_modes: composite solvable by a single skill after all
controller ignores the library and re-derives
assumption_cost: Assumes competence decomposes into callable units; mechanisms that are irreducibly entangled are invisible to this design.
implementation_gap: Needs a composition-capable executor and a withheld-composite task generator.
information_gain: HIGH -- distinguishes 'memory' from 'substrate'.
promotion_gate: Composable library beats all controls except the hand-authored ceiling on withheld composites.
stopping_rule: Preregistered budget; stop early if leakage audit fails.

title: Cross-world transfer of acquired structure
scientific_question: Which acquired structures survive changes of appearance, geometry, dynamics, control mapping and embodiment?
claim_under_test: A substrate-independent skill representation transfers where a world-specific script does not.
why_prometheus: Separates generalized competence from world-specific scripts; the same question our transport experiments (SFE-03/SFE-07) asked in program space.
source_mechanism: SIMA's cross-world instructable agent; Voyager skill schema
minimum_viable_world: One task family rendered in >= 4 variants: visuals, topology, control mapping, object identity, physics, action primitives, embodiment (one axis varied at a time).
controls: matched-compute fresh learner in the target variant
scrambled-mapping control (transfer with a deliberately wrong action mapping)
primary_endpoint: competence in the varied world at fixed compute, transfer minus fresh
secondary_endpoints: fraction of library entries still invoked
anticheat: verify the target variant is not solvable by the source policy by accident (run the frozen source policy first)
falsifier: No axis shows transfer above the fresh baseline, or all axes transfer equally (then the variation is cosmetic).
causal_test: swap only the adapter layer and hold the library fixed; then the inverse
expected_failure_modes: all variants secretly share an action interface
transfer measured before the fresh learner converges
assumption_cost: Assumes an adapter boundary exists at all; agents whose competence IS the interface cannot be tested this way.
donor_code: SIMA 2: NO_PUBLIC_SOURCE (Techne, verified by primary quote). kyegomez/SIMA graded TOY_CLONE. Only the Voyager half has donor code.
implementation_gap: Prometheus must build its own multi-embodiment world variants; no donor supplies them.
information_gain: HIGH -- but blocked until a variant-world harness exists.
promotion_gate: Transfer beats fresh on >= 2 axes with the scrambled-mapping control at baseline.
stopping_rule: Stop if the frozen source policy already solves the variants (design invalid).

title: Generated world curriculum vs its controls
scientific_question: Does adaptive world generation produce more cumulative capability than static, random-procedural, human, novelty-only or difficulty-only generation?
claim_under_test: Adaptive generation expands the reachable competence frontier faster than any single-signal control.
why_prometheus: Directly tests whether Engine Five needs a learned generator or whether our procedural worlds suffice.
source_mechanism: Genie-like learned interactive worlds; OMNI-EPIC learnability/interestingness; POET environment mutation
minimum_viable_world: A parameterised world family where a generator can propose worlds and an oracle can measure reachability; photorealism explicitly out of scope.
controls: held-out ground-truth worlds not produced by any generator
primary_endpoint: expansion of the reachable competence frontier on held-out worlds
anticheat: held-out worlds generated by an independent process
detect generator-specific loopholes (agent success that collapses on held-out variants)
falsifier: Adaptive generation matches random procedural on held-out worlds.
causal_test: swap the generator mid-run between arms and observe whether the frontier follows the generator or the learner
expected_failure_modes: generator collapses onto learner weaknesses (see G-9)
assumption_cost: Learned world models inherit their training distribution; a generated curriculum can only pose what its prior can express. Counter-arm: procedural generator with an explicitly wider support.
donor_code: Genie 1/2/3: NO_PUBLIC_SOURCE (Techne). Open substitutes ranked by Techne: open-oasis, MineWorld, Matrix-Game. OMNI-EPIC and POET repos verified in the catalogue.
implementation_gap: All open substitutes are video-first world models; adapting one to a measurable task world is the real work, and may be cheaper to replace with a parametric generator.
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- high scientific value, but the donor gap is the largest in this set.
promotion_gate: Adaptive beats every control on held-out frontier expansion at equal compute.
stopping_rule: Stop if the generator cannot produce a held-out-valid world within the pilot budget.

title: Closed competence loop: is later progress causally dependent on earlier structure?
scientific_question: Does the generate-attempt-acquire-persist-harden loop produce progress that causally depends on retained structures?
claim_under_test: Removing accumulated structure late in a run collapses competence; equal-size irrelevant structure does not restore it.
why_prometheus: This is the operational definition of cumulative, as opposed to merely long.
source_mechanism: Voyager loop; OMNI-EPIC task selection
minimum_viable_world: Same world as F5-0/F5-1 with a task ladder whose upper rungs are unreachable without lower-rung structure.
primary_endpoint: competence drop after late-run library replacement (per treatment)
secondary_endpoints: dependency depth in the skill graph
anticheat: verify the upper rungs are not solvable from scratch at the same compute (run a fresh learner at the ablation point)
falsifier: Competence is unchanged by library replacement, i.e. progress was not cumulative.
causal_test: the ablation IS the causal test; add restoration to show reversibility
expected_failure_modes: controller re-derives structure quickly, masking dependence
assumption_cost: Cumulativeness is defined via removable structures; competence that has diffused into weights is scored as non-cumulative.
implementation_gap: Needs library swap machinery and a fresh-learner comparator at the ablation point.
information_gain: HIGH -- the single most discriminating test in the ladder.
promotion_gate: Collapse under empty/shuffled/irrelevant, recovery under restoration, no collapse under foreign-lineage only if skills are genuinely general.

title: Self-generated tasks and rewards without evaluator collusion
scientific_question: Can a system generate productive training objectives for itself without merely exploiting its own evaluator?
claim_under_test: Generated task + generated reward yields competence that survives independent evaluation.
why_prometheus: Our doctrine forbids an LLM adjudicating its own science; this measures the size of the effect that rule prevents.
source_mechanism: SIMA 2 self-generated objectives; OMNI-EPIC interestingness; AI Scientist self-evaluation
minimum_viable_world: Any world with an independent, frozen external scorer that the generator cannot read or modify.
controls: frozen external scorer as ground truth for all arms
primary_endpoint: competence under the independent frozen scorer
secondary_endpoints: divergence between self-reported and independent scores
anticheat: scorer state isolated from the generator
detect reward hacking by scoring frozen replays
log every evaluator read
falsifier: Generated-reward arms match external-reward arms under independent evaluation (no collusion penalty, no benefit).
causal_test: swap the evaluator at the end and re-score all arms
telemetry: self-score vs independent score per episode
assumption_cost: Generated rewards privilege measurable objectives; unmeasurable competence is invisible and will be selected away.
donor_code: SIMA 2 no source; OMNI-EPIC verified repo; AI Scientist verified repo
implementation_gap: Build the independent scorer harness; this is reusable instrumentation for AS-1/AS-2.
information_gain: HIGH -- measures our most load-bearing doctrinal assumption.
promotion_gate: Self-generated arms retain >= external arms under the independent scorer.
stopping_rule: Stop on detected scorer leakage; freeze the specimen first.

title: Open-ended reachability: new kinds, not just better scores
scientific_question: Does the closed loop keep exposing new KINDS of reachable behaviour, or only improve within a fixed ontology?
claim_under_test: Behaviour categories discovered post hoc keep appearing over run time rather than saturating.
why_prometheus: Open-endedness claims need a measure that is not defined in advance by us.
source_mechanism: AURORA learned descriptors; ASAL foundation-model search; Atlas/Harmonia anomaly machinery
minimum_viable_world: Any long F5-4 run with full behavioural telemetry.
controls: shuffled-time control for the descriptor model
synthetic run with known category count (positive control for the discovery method)
primary_endpoint: rate of new behaviour clusters per unit compute, discovered by descriptors fitted AFTER the run
anticheat: descriptors fitted without access to task labels
cluster count validated on the synthetic positive control
falsifier: New-cluster rate saturates in the closed loop as fast as in the static control.
causal_test: refit descriptors on shuffled time; clusters must disappear
assumption_cost: Learned descriptors impose their own geometry; alien behaviour that the embedding cannot separate is scored as 'no new kind'.
donor_code: QDax/pyribs verified; AURORA implementation to be confirmed by the catalogue top-up
implementation_gap: Descriptor pipeline + cluster-stability test (shared with QD-3/QD-4 and RA-2).
information_gain: MEDIUM -- depends on descriptor validity; the synthetic positive control decides.
promotion_gate: New-cluster rate exceeds the static control with the positive control passing.
stopping_rule: Stop if the synthetic positive control fails (method invalid).

title: Environment-selection law shoot-out on one organism population
scientific_question: Which environment-selection mechanism expands the reachable capability frontier fastest at equal compute?
claim_under_test: Selection law, not environment mutation, drives frontier expansion.
why_prometheus: All four Prometheus engines use fixed or procedural environments; this is the cheapest test of whether that is a limitation.
source_mechanism: POET, PLR, ACCEL, PAIRED, DRED, MCC, OMNI-EPIC learnability, plus Archaeon's own selector
target_engine: Nestor GraphWorld (same population under different laws) or SFE
minimum_viable_world: An existing Nestor world family with a parametrised generator and a held-out set.
controls: identical organism population and seeds across laws
held-out worlds from an independent generator
primary_endpoint: held-out solve rate at equal environment steps
anticheat: held-out worlds never enter any curriculum
detect regret/learnability estimators reading held-out state
falsifier: All laws within seed variance on held-out frontier.
causal_test: replace the learner mid-run and measure which curricula still work (UED-5)
expected_failure_modes: world family too narrow to separate laws
assumption_cost: Learnability estimators select for what the current learner can almost do; alien-but-hard worlds are systematically suppressed (see UED-8).
prerequisites: a parametrised world generator with a held-out split
donor_code: facebookresearch/dcd (PAIRED/PLR/ACCEL), dramacow/jaxued, uber-research/poet, OMNI-EPIC -- all VERIFIED in the catalogue
implementation_gap: Port the selection laws onto one Prometheus population; the laws are small, the harness is the work.
information_gain: HIGH -- one harness answers UED-1..UED-6 and feeds F5-3 cheaply.
promotion_gate: A law beats random on held-out frontier in >= 2 world families.
evidence_pointers: atlas.ecosystem accel, plr, paired, dred, jaxued

title: Do learnability estimators create invisible selection bias?
scientific_question: Does an interestingness/learnability estimator suppress worlds whose value appears only later?
claim_under_test: Estimator-driven selection discards worlds that would have become stepping stones.
why_prometheus: This is the alienness risk in importing UED wholesale; it also bears on our own detector thresholds.
source_mechanism: OMNI-EPIC interestingness; PLR/ACCEL regret estimators
minimum_viable_world: A world family containing planted late-value worlds (worthless now, valuable after a later capability).
treatments: estimator with a forced exploration floor
controls: planted late-value worlds with known payoff schedule
oracle selector that knows the schedule (ceiling)
primary_endpoint: fraction of planted late-value worlds retained until their payoff epoch
anticheat: planted worlds indistinguishable by surface features (verify with a classifier probe)
falsifier: Estimator retains late-value worlds as well as random selection does.
causal_test: re-run with the retained set forced to include the discarded worlds
expected_failure_modes: planted worlds detectable by a shortcut
payoff schedule too early to discriminate
assumption_cost: The experiment defines value by a planted schedule, which is itself an ontology; genuinely alien late value is not represented.
implementation_gap: Planted-world generator with a hidden payoff schedule (reusable instrumentation).
information_gain: HIGH -- XS-to-S cost, and it can falsify an assumption we are about to import.
promotion_gate: Estimator retains significantly fewer late-value worlds than random, with the probe showing they were not surface-detectable.

title: Generator-learner degenerate co-adaptation
scientific_question: Do generator and learner enter a degenerate loop where worlds collapse onto learner weaknesses?
claim_under_test: Adaptive generation without a diversity floor converges to a narrow world distribution.
why_prometheus: A failure mode Engine Five would inherit; also a risk for Archaeon's frontier scheduler.
source_mechanism: PAIRED minimax-regret dynamics; POET transfer/novelty guards
minimum_viable_world: UED-1 harness with generator capacity high enough to overfit.
primary_endpoint: world-distribution entropy over time and held-out frontier
anticheat: entropy computed on world parameters, not on generator internals
falsifier: No entropy collapse even at high generator capacity.
causal_test: swap in a naive learner; a co-adapted generator should mis-serve it
expected_failure_modes: capacity too low to show collapse
assumption_cost: Entropy on chosen parameters is a proxy; collapse along unparametrised axes is invisible.
implementation_gap: Entropy instrumentation only.
information_gain: MEDIUM -- likely confirms a known risk, but cheap and reusable.
promotion_gate: Entropy collapse reproduced and reversed by the diversity floor.

title: Environment transfer vs environment mutation
scientific_question: Does moving agents between environments matter more than mutating environments?
claim_under_test: POET's transfer step, not its mutation step, carries most of the benefit.
why_prometheus: Tells us which half of POET to import; transfer is far cheaper than a generator.
source_mechanism: POET (mutation + transfer), Enhanced POET, ATEP
minimum_viable_world: A niche set with migration controls (our GraphWorld niches already support this).
primary_endpoint: held-out frontier at equal compute (2x2 factorial)
anticheat: transfer log audited for accidental copying of solutions
falsifier: Only the interaction term matters, or neither factor does.
causal_test: disable transfer late and observe frontier stall
expected_failure_modes: niches too similar for transfer to matter
assumption_cost: Assumes environments are separable into niches; continuous world spaces do not fit.
implementation_gap: Small: a 2x2 switch in the harness.
information_gain: HIGH -- cheap factorial that decides what to import.
promotion_gate: A main effect survives with matched compute.

title: Does MAP-Elites preserve stepping stones our selection loses?
scientific_question: Do archived low-fitness niches later become necessary ancestors of high-fitness solutions?
claim_under_test: Quality-diversity archives retain lineages that our elite-selection loop discards, and those lineages matter later.
why_prometheus: Our GraphWorld already keeps QD cells; this asks whether they pay off, using our own data plus a matched run.
source_mechanism: MAP-Elites, CMA-ME, QDax, pyribs
minimum_viable_world: An existing GraphWorld family run twice: QD archive vs elite-only selection.
treatments: QD with archive pruned each epoch
controls: random-archive control (keep random individuals at the same rate)
primary_endpoint: fraction of final high-fitness solutions whose ancestry passes through a cell that elite-only would have discarded
anticheat: ancestry reconstructed from logged lineage, not inferred
random-archive control rules out 'any memory helps'
falsifier: High-fitness solutions rarely descend from discarded cells, or the random archive does as well.
causal_test: replay with the specific ancestor cells removed
expected_failure_modes: lineage logging incomplete in old runs
assumption_cost: MAP-Elites needs a behavioural partition chosen in advance; stepping stones outside that partition are invisible (QD-3/QD-4 attack exactly this).
implementation_gap: Ancestry reconstruction may need a telemetry addition; check RA-2 first -- old cells.jsonl may already suffice.
information_gain: HIGH -- tests a mechanism we already pay for.
promotion_gate: Archive-dependent ancestry exceeds the random-archive control.
evidence_pointers: primordial/ledger/qd/cells.jsonl (117 cells, not yet indexed -- ATLAS-07)

title: Learned vs human behaviour descriptors
scientific_question: Do learned behaviour descriptors (AURORA-style) outperform our hand-chosen descriptors, and are they stable?
claim_under_test: Unsupervised descriptors find axes our instrumentation missed without destroying historical comparability.
why_prometheus: Our QD cells use human-chosen axes; if learned axes are better, every past archive is under-instrumented.
source_mechanism: AURORA unsupervised descriptors
minimum_viable_world: One GraphWorld family with raw behaviour traces retained.
controls: random projection descriptors of the same dimension
synthetic data with known axes (positive control)
primary_endpoint: coverage and peak fitness per evaluation under each descriptor set
secondary_endpoints: axes discovered that no human axis captures
anticheat: descriptor fit must not see fitness
random-projection control rules out 'any embedding helps'
falsifier: Learned descriptors match random projections, or drift destroys comparability without any coverage gain.
causal_test: re-score an old archive under learned descriptors and check whether ranking changes materially
assumption_cost: Learned descriptors inherit the trace representation; behaviour not expressed in the trace stays invisible.
donor_code: QDax verified; AURORA implementation availability pending the catalogue top-up
implementation_gap: Descriptor pipeline shared with F5-6 and RA-2.
information_gain: HIGH -- and it directly enables RA-2 on old runs.
promotion_gate: Learned descriptors beat human and random-projection on coverage at equal evaluations, with drift quantified.
stopping_rule: Stop if the synthetic positive control fails.

title: Do archived weak lineages become critical after an environment change?
scientific_question: After a world shift, do previously weak archived lineages become the source of the new best solutions?
claim_under_test: Archives are insurance: their value appears only under nonstationarity.
why_prometheus: Our worlds are mostly stationary; if archives only pay under change, our current measurements understate them.
source_mechanism: MAP-Elites archives; POET niche reuse; Flow-Lenia species turnover
minimum_viable_world: A world family with a scheduled, preregistered shift at a fixed epoch.
controls: shift announced vs unannounced (if the selector can see it)
primary_endpoint: post-shift recovery time and peak, by archive policy
secondary_endpoints: ancestry share from pre-shift weak cells
anticheat: shift generated independently of the archive contents
falsifier: Recovery is identical with and without the archive.
causal_test: restore only the weak cells (not the elites) and measure recovery
assumption_cost: Shifts are preregistered and parametric; real nonstationarity may not resemble them.
implementation_gap: Scheduled-shift world wrapper (reusable).
information_gain: HIGH -- could explain why archives look useless in stationary tests.
promotion_gate: Archive-retained arm recovers faster with ancestry traced to pre-shift weak cells.

title: Recombination across distant niches
scientific_question: Does recombining individuals from distant archive cells produce useful novelty, or mostly inviable offspring?
claim_under_test: Cross-niche recombination yields a higher rate of novel viable behaviour than within-niche variation at equal cost.
why_prometheus: Crius already runs a recombination arm with PARTS donors; this generalises the question to archives.
source_mechanism: MAP-Elites variation operators; CycleQD; M2N2 merging
minimum_viable_world: Any archive with a defined distance metric between cells.
controls: viability-matched control (equal number of viable offspring)
primary_endpoint: novel viable behaviours per unit compute
anticheat: novelty measured against the archive as of the parent generation, not the final archive
falsifier: Distant recombination yields no more novelty per compute than within-niche mutation.
causal_test: ablate one parent's contribution (splice back) to attribute the novelty
assumption_cost: Assumes a meaningful genotype crossover exists; representations without it are excluded.
implementation_gap: Recombination operator per representation; Crius already has PARTS splicing.
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- Crius's existing takeover logs may already answer part of it (see RA-4).
promotion_gate: Distant recombination beats within-niche on novel-viable-per-compute.

title: Fixed vs mutable interpreter
scientific_question: Does letting the copying/interpreting machinery itself mutate create qualitatively different evolutionary dynamics?
claim_under_test: A mutable interpreter changes which computations are reachable, not merely how fast they are found.
why_prometheus: Nestor, Bellerophon and Crius all assume a fixed interpreter; this is a foundational assumption test.
source_mechanism: Stringmol (program-program reactions), Tierra/Avida fixed CPUs, Aevol genome structure, BFF soups
minimum_viable_world: A small program soup where the copy operator is itself encoded in the genome and can be mutated.
controls: lethality-matched control (equalise the fraction of viable offspring)
primary_endpoint: set of computations reached (reachability set), not time-to-solution
anticheat: detect runner-provided reproduction
verify offspring arise from executed copies (event log)
falsifier: Reachability sets coincide once mutation rate and viability are matched.
causal_test: freeze the interpreter mid-run in the mutable arm and observe whether reachability stalls
expected_failure_modes: mutable interpreter mostly lethal, so the arm is compute-starved
assumption_cost: Program soups privilege discrete symbolic heredity; continuous-substrate heredity (Lenia-like) is excluded and needs AL-3.
prerequisites: endogenous copy substrate (Nestor Z80-like work may supply it)
donor_code: stringmol, avida, aevol, cubff -- all verified repos in the catalogue
implementation_gap: Mutable-interpreter substrate; Nestor's current campaign may already build the endogenous half.
information_gain: HIGH -- attacks an assumption shared by three engines.
conflicts: Nestor's own Z80 campaign may overlap; coordinate before design
promotion_gate: Reachability differs with matched rates and viability.

title: Evolvable organism boundary
scientific_question: What changes when the boundary of the organism is not fixed by the substrate?
claim_under_test: An evolvable boundary permits phenomena (higher-level individuality, collective reproduction) that a fixed boundary forbids.
why_prometheus: Our organisms have fixed boundaries by construction; this is a precondition for the individuality questions (TI-*).
source_mechanism: Flow-Lenia mass conservation and species; DISHTINY group cells; SCL autopoiesis
target_engine: Nestor NPE or a Lenia-class substrate
minimum_viable_world: A mass-conserving continuous or cellular world where clusters can persist and divide.
primary_endpoint: emergence and persistence of multi-unit reproducing entities
anticheat: entity detection must not presuppose the expected structure (validate the detector on synthetic positives and negatives)
falsifier: No persistent multi-unit entities under any treatment, or they appear equally with a fixed boundary.
causal_test: transplant a candidate entity into a fresh world and measure survival vs its components
assumption_cost: Continuous substrates make discrete lineage bookkeeping hard; our existing lineage tooling may not apply.
implementation_gap: Entity detector with validated controls; this is the crux and is reusable for TI-1.
information_gain: HIGH but risky -- the detector defines the result, so the controls decide whether it means anything.
promotion_gate: Entities detected with validated detector, persisting and transplanting better than components.
stopping_rule: Stop if the detector fails its synthetic controls.

title: Explicit reproduction opcode vs reproduction from local interactions
scientific_question: Does reproduction need a privileged operation, or can it emerge from generic local interactions?
claim_under_test: Emergent reproduction yields a different distribution of replicator architectures than a reproduction opcode.
why_prometheus: Determines whether 'reproduction' should be a substrate primitive in future engines.
source_mechanism: Stringmol reactions; BFF self-replicators from random soups; Squirm3 chemistry
minimum_viable_world: Random-initialised soup with only generic read/write/execute interactions, plus a matched arm with a copy opcode.
controls: seeded replicator (positive control for detection only, never as origin evidence)
primary_endpoint: time to first replicator and architecture diversity of replicators found
anticheat: seeded replicators never counted as spontaneous origin
check for runner-side copying
falsifier: Architecture distributions coincide; the opcode only changes speed.
causal_test: remove the opcode mid-run and test persistence of existing replicators
expected_failure_modes: no spontaneous replicator within budget (report as eligibility, not failure)
assumption_cost: Emergence is scored by a replicator detector; alien self-maintenance that does not copy is missed.
implementation_gap: Mostly configuration of an existing donor; cheapest of the AL family.
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- cubff makes the negative arm nearly free.
promotion_gate: Distinct architecture distributions with matched compute.
stopping_rule: Fixed budget; report eligibility if no replicator appears.

title: When does a collective become the unit of selection?
scientific_question: Can a higher-level unit of selection emerge without an explicit group-fitness term?
claim_under_test: Collective reproduction and specialisation arise from local rules alone when the boundary is evolvable.
why_prometheus: Bears directly on whether mixture-of-experts-like organisation can emerge rather than be designed.
source_mechanism: DISHTINY hierarchical transitions
minimum_viable_world: Spatial world with local resource sharing and heritable cell-level policies; no group fitness term anywhere.
controls: group term arm proves the detector can see group selection
sharing disabled proves it is not an artefact
primary_endpoint: evidence of selection acting at the collective level (validated multilevel-selection statistic)
anticheat: statistic validated on synthetic data with known group selection present and absent
falsifier: No group-level signal without the explicit term, under a statistic that detects it in the positive control.
causal_test: transplant collectives vs matched component sets
expected_failure_modes: runs too short for a transition
assumption_cost: Multilevel-selection statistics carry their own model of individuality; a transition of another kind will not register.
implementation_gap: Statistic + validation harness; DISHTINY itself may be runnable as the substrate.
information_gain: HIGH -- and it is one of the few places an unexpected higher-order structure could appear.
promotion_gate: Group-level signal in the test arm with both controls behaving as required.
stopping_rule: Stop if the positive control shows no signal (instrument invalid).

title: Evolving executable machinery vs parameter-only adaptation
scientific_question: Does evolving code/structure outperform tuning parameters at equal compute, and at what reliability cost?
claim_under_test: Structural (program) change produces larger capability jumps and lower reliability than parameter change.
why_prometheus: Decides whether our future engines should evolve programs or parameters, and what QA that implies.
source_mechanism: FunSearch, AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve, DGM
minimum_viable_world: A task family with a frozen held-out evaluator and a parameterisable baseline solution.
primary_endpoint: held-out performance at equal evaluations
anticheat: held-out evaluator never in the loop
detect evaluator exploitation by re-scoring on a second independent evaluator (EV-8)
falsifier: Program mutation matches parameter search on held-out performance and variance.
causal_test: transplant the evolved program to a sibling task (EV-9)
telemetry: evaluation scores in and out of loop
expected_failure_modes: task too easy for structure to matter
assumption_cost: Program evolution assumes a programmatic representation; competence that is not expressible as code is excluded.
donor_code: OpenEvolve and DGM verified; AlphaEvolve has no runnable code (results repo only); FunSearch official repo verified
implementation_gap: Evaluator harness shared with F5-5 and AS-*; LLM mutation costs need a budget decision.
information_gain: HIGH -- decides whether our next engines evolve programs or parameters, and it is the prerequisite measurement for EV-8's exploitation tax; both answers change what QA an engine needs.
promotion_gate: A difference in held-out performance or variance survives matched evaluations.
stopping_rule: Preregistered evaluation budget or spend cap.

title: What fraction of apparent improvement is evaluator exploitation?
scientific_question: How much of self-modification's measured gain disappears under an independent evaluator?
claim_under_test: A substantial fraction of gains from self-modifying loops is evaluator-specific.
why_prometheus: We have 26 SCIENCE_DEFECT and multiple cheat-control findings already; this quantifies the tax.
source_mechanism: DGM self-modification; AI Scientist self-evaluation; our own cheat controls
minimum_viable_world: EV-1 harness with two independently built evaluators.
treatments: evaluator rotated at a fixed schedule
controls: held-out evaluator built by a different author/process
primary_endpoint: gain retained under the independent evaluator, as a fraction of in-loop gain
anticheat: the experiment IS the anti-cheat measurement; specimens frozen before any patch
falsifier: Retained fraction is near 1 (no exploitation) across loop lengths.
causal_test: patch the exploited channel and re-run to see whether the gain returns legitimately
expected_failure_modes: the two evaluators share a flaw
assumption_cost: Assumes exploitation is detectable by disagreement; correlated blind spots stay invisible.
implementation_gap: Second evaluator must be genuinely independent -- the hard part.
information_gain: HIGH -- and reusable across every engine that scores itself.
promotion_gate: Retained fraction measured with a documented exploit taxonomy.
stopping_rule: Freeze and stop on the first exploit that changes the substrate.

title: Evolution over a skill library vs over whole agents
scientific_question: Is search more effective over an acquired library than over the base agent?
claim_under_test: A library is a better search substrate than a policy: same compute, more improvement.
why_prometheus: If true, the library is not memory but a new evolutionary substrate -- the strongest argument for Engine Five.
source_mechanism: Voyager library + DGM/OpenEvolve program evolution
minimum_viable_world: F5-1 world with a populated library.
primary_endpoint: held-out competence gain per evaluation
anticheat: held-out tasks fixed before search
detect edits that inline test answers
falsifier: Library evolution matches policy evolution per evaluation.
causal_test: transplant evolved library entries into a fresh agent
assumption_cost: Assumes the library is the locus of competence; a controller that ignores it makes the test vacuous.
implementation_gap: Mutation operators over skill payloads.
information_gain: HIGH -- decides the Engine Five kill gate as much as F5-4 does.
promotion_gate: Library search beats policy search per evaluation on held-out tasks.

title: Which memory forms survive a context reset, transfer and compose?
scientific_question: Across memory forms, which survive context reset, transfer between agents, and compose with each other?
claim_under_test: Executable and program-like memories survive and transfer; textual and parametric ones do not, at equal bytes.
why_prometheus: Separates remembering from becoming able; the core of experience-to-competence efficiency.
source_mechanism: Voyager skills; retrieval-augmented memory; option learning; parameter updates
minimum_viable_world: F5-0 world with a fixed competence probe battery.
primary_endpoint: competence retained after context reset, per byte
anticheat: byte accounting audited
probe battery withheld from all memory content
falsifier: All forms perform equally per byte after reset.
causal_test: cross-transplant each form into a naive agent
expected_failure_modes: forms not comparable at equal bytes
assumption_cost: Byte-matching privileges compact symbolic forms; distributed competence is penalised by construction. State this in the readout.
implementation_gap: Ten memory backends is the cost; a 4-form subset (context, retrieval, executable skill, parameter update) is the S-sized version.
information_gain: HIGH -- gives a per-byte competence currency usable by every engine.
promotion_gate: A per-byte ranking with the scrambled controls at baseline.

title: Does consolidation compress episodes into competence, and does compression track generalisation?
scientific_question: Can many episodes be consolidated into a smaller structure that retains competence, and does the compression ratio predict generalisation?
claim_under_test: Compression of experience into structure correlates with held-out generalisation.
why_prometheus: A direct measure of experience-to-competence efficiency, and a candidate promotion signal.
source_mechanism: Skill-library consolidation; model merging (Evolutionary Model Merge, M2N2)
minimum_viable_world: MEM-1 world with long runs and a held-out battery.
controls: random pruning at the same ratio
primary_endpoint: held-out competence per byte after consolidation
anticheat: random-pruning control rules out 'less is more'
falsifier: Consolidation is indistinguishable from random pruning at the same ratio.
causal_test: restore pruned content and measure recovery
expected_failure_modes: consolidation implemented as summarisation, losing executability
assumption_cost: Compression as a proxy for understanding is itself a strong assumption; report it as correlation only.
donor_code: Model-merge repos pending verification in the top-up
implementation_gap: Consolidation operator per memory form.
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- if compression tracks generalisation it gives us a cheap, continuous promotion signal for any engine that accumulates structure; if it does not, it kills a tempting shortcut we would otherwise adopt on intuition.
promotion_gate: Consolidated beats random-pruned at equal ratio.

title: Independent lineages vs shared discovery
scientific_question: Does sharing discoveries between evolutionary branches raise cumulative innovation, or cause monoculture?
claim_under_test: Sharing raises innovation up to a threshold, beyond which diversity and long-run innovation fall.
why_prometheus: Prometheus IS a population of seats sharing fossils; this tests the macro-organism architecture itself.
source_mechanism: Group-evolving agents; POET transfer; island models
minimum_viable_world: N independent lineages on one world family with a controllable sharing channel.
controls: random-payload sharing control (share noise of the same size)
primary_endpoint: cumulative distinct innovations across the population at equal total compute
anticheat: random-payload control rules out 'any perturbation helps'
innovation counted on first appearance, deduplicated by mechanism
falsifier: Sharing changes nothing beyond seed variance, or full sharing dominates at every rate (no monoculture cost).
causal_test: cut the channel mid-run and observe divergence or stagnation
assumption_cost: Assumes innovations are transferable objects; tacit competence that cannot be packaged is invisible.
donor_code: Pending the catalogue top-up for group-evolving agents; POET transfer verified
implementation_gap: Innovation deduplication is the hard part and is reusable for GEA-4 and RA-5.
information_gain: HIGH -- tests our own architecture, not a paper's.
promotion_gate: A sharing-rate optimum, or its absence, established with the random-payload control at baseline.

title: Raw fossils vs extracted organs
scientific_question: Does access to extracted mechanisms beat access to raw ancestors?
claim_under_test: Nyx-extracted organs raise innovation per compute more than Techne raw fossils, which beat no access.
why_prometheus: This is the load-bearing claim of the Techne-to-Nyx pipeline; it has never been tested causally.
source_mechanism: DGM archive selection; fossil injection; Nyx organ extraction
minimum_viable_world: A task family where known historical solutions exist in our fossil vault.
primary_endpoint: innovations per unit compute, and rediscovery cost avoided
secondary_endpoints: fraction of solutions traceable to an injected artefact
anticheat: irrelevant-fossil control
artefacts hashed; solutions diffed against them to detect copying rather than reuse
falsifier: Organ access matches raw fossil access, which matches the irrelevant-fossil control.
causal_test: withdraw access mid-run; measure whether the advantage persists (internalised) or collapses (dependency)
expected_failure_modes: vault coverage too thin for the task family
assumption_cost: Extraction privileges mechanisms that survive being named and packaged; unpackageable advantages are scored as worthless.
donor_code: Internal: techne/fossils (121 fossils, 105 runnable), nyx/atlas organs
implementation_gap: Injection harness; no external donor needed.
information_gain: HIGH -- cheap, internal, and it tests a core architectural bet.
promotion_gate: Ordering (organ > fossil > none) with the irrelevant-fossil control at baseline.

title: Sharing topology: near vs distant niches
scientific_question: Is sharing more productive within related niches or across distant ones?
claim_under_test: Cross-niche sharing produces rarer but larger innovations; within-niche sharing produces more, smaller ones.
why_prometheus: Informs how seats should route findings to each other.
source_mechanism: Island models; POET transfer; QD cross-niche recombination
minimum_viable_world: GEA-1 harness with a niche-distance metric.
primary_endpoint: innovation size distribution by sharing distance
anticheat: distance metric fixed before the run
falsifier: Distance has no effect on innovation size or rate.
causal_test: swap the distance metric and re-run (metric sensitivity)
assumption_cost: Requires a niche metric; if the metric is wrong, the result is about the metric.
implementation_gap: Distance metric definition.
information_gain: MEDIUM -- it refines GEA-1 rather than testing a new assumption, but it is the result that would tell the seats HOW to route findings to each other, which is a standing operational question.
promotion_gate: A distance effect survives the metric-swap check.

title: Branch selection: random vs expected-information-gain
scientific_question: Does information-gain-driven branch selection increase discovery per compute without increasing false discovery?
claim_under_test: EIG selection beats random branch selection on true discoveries per compute at equal false-discovery rate.
why_prometheus: Archaeon's frontier scheduler already selects branches; this tests the selection rule itself.
source_mechanism: AI Scientist branch search; OMNI-EPIC interestingness; our frontier queues
target_engine: Archaeon frontier (or a simulator of it)
minimum_viable_world: A synthetic hypothesis landscape with known ground truth, plus a replay of our own frontier queue decisions.
controls: ground-truth landscape with known true/false hypotheses
primary_endpoint: true discoveries per unit compute at matched false-discovery rate
anticheat: ground truth hidden from the selector
false-discovery rate measured on held-out confirmation
falsifier: EIG matches random at equal compute and FDR.
causal_test: replay our historical frontier decisions under each rule and compare outcomes
assumption_cost: EIG needs a model of the hypothesis space; genuinely alien hypotheses have no prior and are never selected.
prerequisites: frontier decision log (already in the index)
implementation_gap: Synthetic landscape generator; the replay half needs no new donor.
information_gain: HIGH -- the replay arm uses data we already have.
promotion_gate: A rule beats random on discoveries per compute at matched FDR.

title: Can an autonomous system recover a hypothesis it previously rejected?
scientific_question: Do automated campaigns ever revisit and revive correctly-rejected-then-wrong rejections?
claim_under_test: Without an explicit revival mechanism, rejected hypotheses are never recovered, even when later evidence supports them.
why_prometheus: Our own loops park and supersede; this measures whether parking is reversible in practice.
source_mechanism: AI Scientist branch pruning; our frontier suppressions and CW01 stasis records
minimum_viable_world: Synthetic landscape where a hypothesis becomes true only after a later capability exists.
controls: ground truth with known revival epoch
primary_endpoint: recovery rate of revivable hypotheses
anticheat: revival schedule hidden from the selector
falsifier: Permanent pruning recovers as well as scheduled revival.
causal_test: compare against our own historical suppression records (PROTEUS-46, CW01 stasis)
expected_failure_modes: revival epoch never reached in budget
assumption_cost: Revivability is defined by the planted schedule.
implementation_gap: Shares AS-3 infrastructure.
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- cheap once AS-3 exists.
promotion_gate: Recovery-rate difference established.

title: REANALYSIS: did frontier queue pools act as a curriculum?
scientific_question: In our own DEEP FRONTIER history, did pool/priority assignment predict subsequent detector firings better than chance?
claim_under_test: Existing queue decisions already contain a measurable curriculum effect.
why_prometheus: Answers part of UED-1 with data we already hold; costs compute we already spent.
source_mechanism: PLR/ACCEL prioritisation concepts applied post hoc
minimum_viable_world: None -- existing records.
primary_endpoint: firings and evaluations per queued item by pool, vs permutation null
anticheat: null built by permuting assignment within time windows
falsifier: Pool assignment carries no signal beyond the permutation null.
causal_test: none possible retrospectively; state it as association only
telemetry: already indexed: 442 queue items, 22 RUN attempts, 1,196 detector_firing facts
expected_failure_modes: too few RUN events to separate pools (likely; report eligibility)
assumption_cost: Retrospective association only; no causal claim is licensed.
implementation_gap: A single SQL/notebook pass over atlas.*
information_gain: MEDIUM -- likely underpowered, but it costs almost nothing and sizes the real experiment.
promotion_gate: Report with eligibility count stated first.

title: REANALYSIS: learned descriptors over old GraphWorld and CW01 runs
scientific_question: Do AURORA-style descriptors fitted post hoc reveal behaviour clusters, transitions or anomalies our original metrics missed?
claim_under_test: Our historical archives contain structure our hand-chosen metrics did not capture.
why_prometheus: The operator's explicit request: find missed science in what we already ran.
source_mechanism: AURORA unsupervised descriptors
target_engine: Atlas analysis over nestor.graphworld and nestor.cw01
minimum_viable_world: None -- existing rows and QD cells.
primary_endpoint: count of behaviour clusters not separable under the original metrics, validated against the synthetic control
anticheat: descriptor fit blind to outcome labels
synthetic positive control must pass first
falsifier: No cluster structure beyond random projections.
causal_test: none retrospectively; flag candidates for prospective test
telemetry: needs primordial/ledger/rows/* and qd/cells.jsonl indexed first (ATLAS-07)
assumption_cost: The embedding's geometry decides what counts as a cluster.
implementation_gap: Descriptor pipeline (shared with QD-3, F5-6).
information_gain: HIGH -- this is the highest-value reanalysis in the set.
promotion_gate: Clusters survive the random-projection and shuffled-time controls.
stopping_rule: Stop if the synthetic control fails.

title: REANALYSIS: evaluator-exploitation census across campaigns
scientific_question: Across all campaigns, how often did organisms or agents exploit the evaluator, and which control caught it?
claim_under_test: Cheat controls, not positive controls or human reading, caught most exploitation.
why_prometheus: Quantifies the value of our cheat-control doctrine and feeds EV-8's design.
source_mechanism: Our own defect ledgers and control facts
minimum_viable_world: None -- existing records.
treatments: census by campaign, category and detecting control
controls: classification validated on a hand-labelled sample
primary_endpoint: exploitation events per campaign and detecting mechanism
anticheat: hand-label a sample to measure classifier error before trusting counts
falsifier: Exploits are too rare or too unevenly recorded to support any rate claim (report as such).
causal_test: none; descriptive
telemetry: already indexed: 218 defects, 610 control facts, 308 failure_mode facts
assumption_cost: Only recorded exploits count; undetected ones are invisible by construction, which is the finding's main limit.
implementation_gap: One analysis pass plus hand labelling.
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- cheap, and it directly sizes EV-8.
promotion_gate: Census published with classifier error stated.

title: REANALYSIS: Crius PARTS takeovers as a cross-niche recombination result
scientific_question: Do Crius's existing recombination-arm takeover logs already show whether donor splices beat within-lineage variation?
claim_under_test: The C2 recombination arm contains a usable answer to QD-9 at zero additional compute.
why_prometheus: Prefer reanalysis before rerun; Crius ran the arm for another purpose.
source_mechanism: MAP-Elites recombination; Crius PARTS donors
minimum_viable_world: None -- existing takeovers.jsonl and PARTS diagnostics.
controls: paired common-random streams already used by Crius
primary_endpoint: takeover rate and selective value by donor distance
anticheat: use Crius's own paired streams; do not re-derive significance from selected populations
falsifier: Donor distance has no association with takeover rate.
causal_test: none retrospectively; flag for prospective QD-9
expected_failure_modes: arm not yet run to completion
assumption_cost: Crius's distance metric is inherited wholesale.
prerequisites: Crius C2 arm complete; ask Crius in comms before analysing
implementation_gap: Index Crius campaign 2 first (Atlas does not yet harvest Crius).
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- it may answer QD-9 for free from an arm Crius ran for another purpose; the risk is that rung and donor distance are confounded, in which case it only sizes the prospective run.
promotion_gate: Association reported with eligibility counts.

title: REANALYSIS: rediscovery rate across seats and lineages
scientific_question: How often have independent Prometheus lineages rediscovered the same mechanism?
claim_under_test: Rediscovery is common enough to justify the fossil/organ pipeline (GEA-4).
why_prometheus: Sizes the value of sharing before we build more sharing machinery.
source_mechanism: Group-evolving agents; our own mechanism ledgers
minimum_viable_world: None -- Nyx mechanism ledger, Techne fossils, campaign conclusions.
treatments: mechanism-level deduplication across campaigns and seats
controls: name-only matching as a weak baseline
primary_endpoint: count of mechanisms independently arrived at more than once
secondary_endpoints: whether the later one cited the earlier
anticheat: dedup validated on labelled pairs before counting
falsifier: Rediscovery is rare, weakening the case for organ sharing.
causal_test: none; descriptive
telemetry: atlas.conclusion (468), mechanism_claim facts (99), nyx mechanism ledger
expected_failure_modes: mechanism descriptions too heterogeneous to dedup reliably
assumption_cost: Dedup by description privileges mechanisms that were named; unnamed convergence is missed.
implementation_gap: Mechanism dedup (shared with GEA-1).
information_gain: MEDIUM-HIGH -- decides how much GEA machinery is worth building.
promotion_gate: Rate reported with dedup accuracy.
